sections.h2: What kind of place is Bacon County?
sections.html:
Bacon County is a rural, low-density county in southeast Georgia, and Alma is its seat. Wikipedia, citing Census Bureau area figures, gives it 286 square miles: 259 of land and 27 of water, or 9.5% water. The same entry notes the amendment that created the county was ratified by voters on November 3, 1914.

Streams define the map. Western and central Bacon County drains toward the Satilla River, and the eastern edge feeds the Little Satilla. Neighbors are Appling to the northeast, Pierce to the southeast, Ware to the south, Coffee to the west and Jeff Davis to the northwest. Alma is the lone city. Rockingham is a census-designated place, and Coffee and Sessoms are unincorporated.

QuickFacts estimates 11,070 residents in mid-2025, nearly the same as the 11,140 counted in the 2020 census, with roughly 39 people per square mile. A listing here is usually a house on a country lot, often with a well, a septic tank and room for outbuildings.

sections.h2: How do home values and incomes look in Bacon County?
sections.html:
This is one of the least expensive housing markets in Georgia. For 2020-2024, QuickFacts shows a $101,400 median for homes their owners live in, and 68.6% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Fourteen permits in all of 2025 tells you almost no new houses are being built, so a buyer shopping here compares your property to older stock. And with 93.3% of residents staying put year to year, turnover is slow. Pricing your place against what recently closed nearby, not against a state average, is the realistic move.

sections.h2: Which counter handles what in Alma?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner and the assessors work from the Bacon County Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. The tax commissioner's website posts one phone line, 912-632-5614, and office hours of 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

  • Suite 101, tax commissioner: bills, payments, liens and mobile home permits
  • Suite 101, tax assessors: values, returns, exemptions and appeals
  • Suite 200, Clerk of Superior Court: copies of deeds

Parcel lookups run through qPublic. The commissioner's site also reminds visitors that its pages are general information and that the Official Code of Georgia controls.

sections.h2: When is the Bacon County bill due, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
The usual due date is November 15, and mail goes out at least 60 days beforehand. The date on your bill wins, since the county says it can shift.

You may pay in two parts, but whatever remains after the due date keeps collecting charges. Envelopes need a postmark on or before the deadline, and weekend or holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. A drive-up drop box stands on the right side of the front lot. Cards carry a 2.75% processor fee, minimum $2.00.

  • Monthly interest: the bank prime loan rate plus 3%
  • Penalty: 5% of the tax, first applied 120 days after the due date, then every 120 days, topping out at 20%
  • Homesteaded parcels with a bill under $500 escape the penalty
  • Mobile and manufactured homes: due April 1, with a 10% penalty

sections.h2: Can a tax lien follow a Bacon County sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the bill stays open. A bill unpaid 30 days past its due date can be turned into a FiFa, a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket. The county cautions that such a lien can sit on a credit file for seven years or more, and that it mails delinquent notices only at intervals, so call before sending a payoff.

By law the lien goes in the name of whoever held the property on January 1. A change of name requires paperwork: carry the signed closing statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date, and the office can record the lien against the new owner. If a bill reaches you after you sold, hand it to the buyer.

  1. Ask Suite 101 for a written balance.
  2. Have the title company pay it from your proceeds.
  3. Keep your settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Bacon County value?
sections.html:
Count 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Within that window, put the dispute in writing to the assessors on the state's uniform appeal form, stating one of four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption.

The same filing names the track you choose. With the Board of Equalization, the assessors may revise the value first, and you then get 30 days to answer an amended notice; unresolved appeals go to the board for a hearing, and Superior Court is the next stop. A hearing officer track exists for non-homestead real estate above a value threshold. Arbitration requires a certified appraisal and ends the matter.

Separately, you can use January 1 through April 1 to file a return stating your own value. Real estate returns renew themselves each year, while personal property returns need filing annually.

sections.h2: Which breaks can lower a Bacon County bill?
sections.html:
Homestead is the main one. The state constitution sets a baseline, and Bacon County layers its own exemptions on top, with the higher number controlling. To claim it you must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and your application must arrive by April 1 of the year you first claim; the exemption then renews itself.

  • Age 62 or older with household income of $15,000 or less: deferral of tax on the homestead
  • Qualifying farmland: assessed at 30% rather than 40%
  • Conservation use and forest land: current-use valuation under a covenant of 10 or 15 years
  • Historic and brownfield programs: filed in the same January to April window

Call 912-632-5614 for the local amounts and what proof to bring. Claiming homestead on a second property anywhere, in or out of Georgia, is unlawful.

sections.h2: What is a sensible order of steps for selling with tax due?
sections.html:
Begin with the number. Find out what is owed for each open year, whether a FiFa exists, and, if the house is a mobile home, whether the April 1 permit tax is paid. Then decide whether to pay it ahead of listing or at the closing table.

Inherited houses, rentals and vacant properties often carry several unpaid years, and a title search will surface every recorded lien. If your land sits in a conservation or forest program, ask the assessors what the covenant demands of a new owner before you list, since a buyer will ask.

faqs.q: What share of market value is taxed in Bacon County?
faqs.a: Forty percent of fair market value is the assessed value, and exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate is applied. The county commissioners and the school board set the rate each year.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Bacon County bill?
faqs.a: Pay at Suite 101 of the Government Building in Alma, by mail with a postmark on or before the deadline, in the drop box, or online with a card. Questions go to 912-632-5614.

faqs.q: Does selling split the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: Your closing statement does that, not the county. The tax commissioner asks you to bring the signed statement to Suite 101 within 90 days after the due date if you want a lien recorded against the buyer.

faqs.q: Is there a refund if I sell in March?
faqs.a: No. Georgia's Department of Revenue says the owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year, and it allows no refund for a part-year owner.

faqs.q: Who sends the notice of my home's value?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors in the same building. Call 912-632-5614, and mind the 45-day clock that starts on the date printed on the notice.
